subject: QTL very close to each other and %Var explained

messages.author: ef49ed6122073bff
messages.subject: QTL very close to each other and %Var explained
parts:
Hi,

In my multiple QTL scan for an F2 population, I got two pairs of QTL about 1 cM apart on the same linkage group. From reading previous posts, I went to check if there are outlier individuals at these markers that led to these closely located peaks. In one case, it is easy to identity an outlier individual for genotype AA that is present for marker at 26.5 but not for marker at 27(see chr5pos26.5 and chr5pos27). After excluding this one individual, the QTL at 26.5 dropped out. 

For another pair of peaks, however, it is not so easy to pick out any outlier that is present at one marker but not the other. The phenotypic effect is much smaller and not so clean to begin with. Both had LOD score around 7 from drop one function in a multiple QTL model. The phenotypic distribution for the three genotypes are very similar at both markers (see chr5pos0 and chr5pos1), and both slightly skewed in the same way. Do you have any suggestion on what may have caused this pair of QTL to be so close? 

My second question regards %var explained in a multiple QTL model. I found that the %var explained of the full model (with no interaction terms) is not the sum of the %var explained by each marker from the drop one QTL at a time ANOVA table. Typically it is greater than the sum. I wonder what is the explanation for this discrepancy, and what is your suggestion if we want to report both %var explained by each marker, and %var of the full model.

Many thanks!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] QTL very close to each other and %Var explained
parts:
The issue of selecting a pair of very tightly linked QTL won't go away completely by clipping off the individuals' with extreme genotypes. So rather than omitting individuals, I'd be inclined to just drop the pair of QTL from the model, if you think they are an artifact.

And rather than look at the phenotype vs genotype distribution at each individual marker, I'd want to look at the phenotypes broken up into the 9 possible two-locus genotypes. I'd expect that one of the recombinant classes has one or a few individuals with high or low phenotypes.

Regarding your second question: the % var explained in the drop-one-QTL table is a transformation of the LOD score comparing the model with all of the QTL to the model with that one QTL dropped. The % var explained from the full model is a transformation of the LOD score comparing the full model with all QTL to the model with no QTL. They overall % var generally won't be equal to the sum of the individual values. And results in the drop-one-QTL table are really only meaningful in the case of unlinked QTL.

karl

messages.subject: Re: QTL very close to each other and %Var explained
parts:
Hi Dr. Broman,

Many thanks! It makes sense but I have a general question about identifying linked QTL. When there are a pair of QTL <0.5 cM apart, it's very likely at least one of them is an artifact. It gets less clear when the model identifies 2 QTL, say, 10 cM apart on the same linkage group. In this case, what's your suggestion on distinguishing whether they are real linked QTL or artifacts. Are there formal steps we can follow?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] QTL very close to each other and %Var explained
parts:
The pairs of very tightly linked QTL that I see are generally QTL linked in repulsion, with effects of opposite sign. And I'd think they're either both real or both artifacts, so I wouldn't exclude one but rather both.

The key thing to look at, in deciding whether the QTL can be trusted or not, is the recombinant individuals. And I'd want to have at least two markers between them. If there are just one or two animals that have different genotypes at the two QTL, definitely think artifact. If there are 5-10 or more recombinant individuals, I'd be much more confident about the QTL.

It's hard to put a distance threshold on this, because it depends on the sample size. If you have 1000 individuals, you can more confidently identify tightly linked QTL, than if you have just 100 individuals.

karl
